req.title: Task deletion persists
req.statement: The system shall remove deleted rows so subsequent GET returns 404 for that id.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that deleting a task must persist the removal so that a subsequent GET returns 404. I design tests covering: (1) positive EP — delete an existing task returns 204 and subsequent GET returns 404; (2) negative NEG — delete a non-existent task returns 404 immediately; (3) boundary BVA — delete the lowest valid id (id=1) and highest valid id (id=20) to catch off-by-one mutations in id routing; (4) STC — state transition: task exists → DELETE → task absent, verified by GET; (5) DT — double-delete (idempotency failure path) returns 404 on second attempt. All tests use in-process FastAPI TestClient with a fresh SQLite in-memory database seeded with the specified fixture rows, ensuring determinism and isolation.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_task_returns_204_and_subsequent_get_returns_404
preconditions: Database contains task with id=5 (title='Write project report', completed=false)
TestClient is initialised with in-memory SQLite
actions: POST /tasks/ to create a known task and capture its id
expected: DELETE returns HTTP 204 with no body
GET response body contains detail mentioning the id
trace: R-TASK-023: deleted rows must be removed so subsequent GET returns 404
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import get_db
from app import models

engine = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
TestingSessionLocal = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine)

def override_get_db():
    db = TestingSessionLocal()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
client = TestClient(app)

create_resp = client.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Write project report", "description": "Signal cascade", "completed": False})
assert create_resp.status_code == 201
task_id = create_resp.json()["id"]

del_resp = client.delete(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
assert del_resp.status_code == 204
assert del_resp.content == b""

get_resp = client.get(f"/tasks/{task_id}")
assert get_resp.status_code == 404
assert str(task_id) in get_resp.json()["detail"]

app.dependency_overrides.clear()

tests.name: test_delete_task_does_not_affect_other_tasks
preconditions: Two tasks exist in the database
Only one is targeted for deletion
actions: Create task A and task B
GET /tasks/{id_B} — must still be 200 with correct data
expected: GET task B returns 200 with title matching what was created

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from app.main import app
from app.database import get_db
from app import models

engine6 = create_engine("sqlite:///:memory:", connect_args={"check_same_thread": False})
TestingSessionLocal6 = sessionmaker(autocommit=False, autoflush=False, bind=engine6)
models.Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine6)

def override_get_db6():
    db = TestingSessionLocal6()
    try:
        yield db
    finally:
        db.close()

app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db6
client6 = TestClient(app)

ra = client6.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Pay electricity bill", "completed": True})
assert ra.status_code == 201
id_a = ra.json()["id"]

rb = client6.post("/tasks/", json={"title": "Organize desk", "completed": False})
assert rb.status_code == 201
id_b = rb.json()["id"]

del_a = client6.delete(f"/tasks/{id_a}")
assert del_a.status_code == 204

get_a = client6.get(f"/tasks/{id_a}")
assert get_a.status_code == 404

get_b = client6.get(f"/tasks/{id_b}")
assert get_b.status_code == 200
assert get_b.json()["title"] == "Organize desk"
assert get_b.json()["completed"] == False
assert get_b.json()["id"] == id_b
